text.p: Brazil's Unibanco Holdings, Unibanco and Uniao de Bancos Brasileiros said Thursday they were starting a conversion offer letting shareholders switch pairs of preferred and common shares into newly issued units.
The company said in a statement that the new units would be identical to those sold in a $1.23 billion global secondary offering.
"If all current shareholders convert their shares, the present float in units of approximately $1.5 billion would nearly double," it said.
The statement said the units would have a greater liquidity than the individual classes of Unibanco shares outstanding.
There is no limit on the number of preferred shares that can be accepted in the offer.

"However, the ability of Unibanco and Unibanco Holdings to accept tenders in pairs of Unibanco common shares will depend on the number of Unibanco preferred shares tendered and not withdrawn in the conversion offer."
Unibanco's American Depositary Receipts closed Wednesday at 36-2/16.
